faq.question: What is tortellini in brodo?
faq.answer: Tortellini in brodo is Bologna’s most traditional pasta dish — tiny hand-folded tortellini stuffed with prosciutto, mortadella, Parmigiano Reggiano, pork, egg, and nutmeg, served in rich capon or chicken broth. Purists consider it the only proper way to eat tortellini, earning it the nickname ‘re delle minestre’ (king of soups). The Dotta Confraternita Del Tortellino regulates the exact size — max 2g each, seven should fit on one tablespoon.

faq.question: How much does tortellini cost in Bologna?
faq.answer: A plate of tortellini in brodo at a trattoria typically costs €10–€16. Upscale spots like Da Sandro al Navile charge €14–€20. Budget options like Trattoria del Rosso serve tortellini for €8–€12. A full meal with wine runs €25–€45 per person at most trattorias.

faq.question: What is the difference between tortellini and tortelloni?
faq.answer: Tortellini are small (max 2g each) with a meat filling of prosciutto, mortadella, and Parmigiano. Tortelloni are larger and typically stuffed with ricotta and spinach. Tortellini are served in brodo (broth); tortelloni usually with butter and sage or ragù.

faq.question: When is the best time to eat tortellini in Bologna?
faq.answer: Available year-round, but most special October–March when the warm broth hits different. Christmas is peak tortellini season — it’s the traditional Christmas Day meal across Emilia-Romagna. Tortellini in crema parmigiana or ragù are popular in warmer weather.

faq.question: Should I add Parmigiano to tortellini in brodo?
faq.answer: Traditionally, no. The filling already contains aged Parmigiano Reggiano, so adding more is considered unnecessary. Many restaurants will offer it anyway. For your first bowl, try it without — taste the balance the chef intended.

faq.question: Where do locals eat tortellini in Bologna?
faq.answer: Locals favor spots slightly outside the tourist center: Trattoria di Via Serra in Bolognina and Da Sandro al Navile are neighborhood favorites. In the center, Da Cesari and Grassilli are well-respected. For a day trip, Trattoria da Amerigo in Savigno (Michelin-starred) and Antica Osteria del Mirasole are worth the drive.

faq.question: Can I buy fresh tortellini to take home from Bologna?
faq.answer: Yes! Trattoria da Me has a pasta window at Via San Felice 52/A where you can buy handmade tortellini and watch them being rolled. Paolo Atti & Figli and Tamburini on Via Caprarie are other well-known spots. Fresh tortellini keeps 2–3 days refrigerated or can be frozen.
